fields.meta_description: A conversational landing page asks one question per screen and branches on each answer. See four examples, then build your own by prompt.
fields.h1: Build a Conversational Landing Page, One Question at a Time
fields.hero_description: Build a conversational landing page that asks one question per screen, branches on answers, and saves replies to your database.
fields.features_subheading: Each screen asks one thing. The answer picks the next screen, lands in your database, and alerts a rep when a lead is worth a call.
fields.feature_1:
One question on each screen

Describe the questions in order, and Emergent builds a page that shows them one per screen, with a progress bar and a back button. Reword any of the questions later by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
The next question picked by the last answer

Name the answers that change the path, such as more than 50 employees. The page skips questions that do not apply and sends each visitor to the end screen their answers lead to.
fields.feature_3:
Every reply saved as a row

Each conversation lands as one row in a database you own, with every answer in its own column and the time it came in. Unfinished ones are saved too, up to the last answer given.
fields.feature_4:
A Slack message for leads that qualify

Set the answers that make a lead worth a call, and the rep who owns it gets a Slack message or an email with the answers. The app can also send each lead to any CRM with an API.
fields.feature_5:
Drop-off counted at each question

A dashboard shows how many visitors reached each question and how many left there. When one question loses more people than the others, you see which one and can move it or cut it.
fields.feature_6:
Hosted on your domain, or exported

Publish the page on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep working on it there.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every lead over 50 employees books with sales

Paystead Payroll asks four questions, one per screen. A company with more than 50 employees gets a calendar to book a sales call, and account executive Ofelia Brandt gets a Slack message with the answers. Smaller companies get the free trial link. This week, 41 of 186 finished conversations went to sales.
fields.tab_content_2:
The phone question moved after it lost 31 visitors

Shingleford Roofing in Omaha asks five questions before it quotes a job, and the phone number used to come second. This month, 300 visitors started and 214 finished. The dashboard showed the phone question losing 31 of the 86 who quit, more than any other. The owner made it optional and moved it to the last screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
One answer puts first-timers in Saturday's intro class

Talusridge Climbing in Boulder opens with one question: New to climbing? A visitor who taps Yes is offered the Saturday 10:00 intro class, where 6 of 9 spots are taken, and books with a name and email. A visitor who taps No goes to a belay check booking. Each booking is saved with the answer.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three answers pick one of six samplers

Tealark Tea asks about caffeine, flavor, and brewing, one screen at a time. The answers point to one of six samplers. Low caffeine, floral, and loose leaf lead to Evening Garden, at $18. This month, 1,240 visitors answered all three questions, and 312 of them bought the sampler they were shown.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Conversational Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a conversational landing page that asks the right questions in order and saves each answer, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one result for the conversation
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the conversation has to produce, such as a booked call or a quote request. Every question should earn its place toward that one result. A page that tries to qualify a lead and sell a product at once asks too much of a visitor.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start with a question a visitor can answer in one tap, such as the type of job or whether they are new. Hold questions that ask for effort or trust, such as a phone number, until the visitor has already answered a few.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down every question you want, then cut each one that changes neither the outcome nor the next screen. Aim for five or fewer. If a detail can wait for the follow-up call, leave it off the page and ask it then.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a branch only when an answer changes what the visitor should see next, such as company size deciding between a sales call and a trial. Every branch is another path to test, so keep the map small enough to click through in a few minutes.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask for contact details near the end
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the email or phone question late, after the visitor has seen that the answers matter. Make a phone number optional unless someone calls every lead. Save partial answers, so a visitor who quits still shows you where they stopped.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Offer the plain form as well
fields.howto_step_6_des: Some visitors prefer to see every question at once. Add a link on the first screen that opens the same questions as one form, writing to the same table. Compare how many finish each version before you pick the default.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe each question, every branch, and the end screens in one prompt. Emergent builds the page and its database, then rewords a question or adds a branch when you ask. Answer every path yourself before you send traffic to the page.

faq_plan.q: What is a conversational landing page?
faq_plan.a: A conversational landing page asks visitors one question at a time, in a chat-like sequence, instead of showing a long form all at once. Each answer can change the next question, and the page ends on a result, for example a sales call booked or a product recommended.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a conversational landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write the questions in the order a person would ask them, mark which answers change the path, and decide where each path ends. With Emergent's AI landing page builder, you describe that in one prompt and get the page, its branches, and a database for the answers.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a conversational landing page ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask as few as the result needs; five or fewer is a sensible target for a lead or quote page. Count only questions that change the outcome or the next screen. A roofer needs the job type before quoting, while the gutter color can wait.

faq_plan.q: Is a conversational landing page the same as a chatbot?
faq_plan.a: Not necessarily. A conversational landing page can follow a script you write: fixed questions, set answer choices, and branches you define, with no free-text replies to interpret. Because every visitor who gives the same answers sees the same path, you can test each path before launch.

faq_plan.q: When should I use a conversational landing page instead of a regular form?
faq_plan.a: Use one when the right next step depends on the visitor's answers, such as sending large companies to sales and small ones to a trial. If every visitor gets the same follow-up, a short form on one screen is quicker to fill in. Test both when you are unsure.

faq_plan.q: What should a conversational landing page template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with an opening question that takes one tap, then the questions that decide the path, a contact question near the end, and one end screen per outcome. Show visitors how far along they are. The app Emergent builds saves every answer to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I see where visitors drop off in a conversational landing page?
faq_plan.a: Save each answer as it comes in, not only when the visitor finishes. Then count, for every question, how many visitors reached it and how many left there. The app Emergent builds can show those counts on a dashboard, where the question that loses the most visitors is easy to spot.

faq_plan.q: Can a conversational landing page send leads to my CRM?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the CRM has an API. The app Emergent builds can create a contact there for each finished conversation, with every answer mapped to its own field, and can update that record when the visitor books a call.

faq_plan.q: Should a conversational landing page ask for an email first or last?
faq_plan.a: Ask near the end when the conversation gives the visitor something first, such as a quote range or a product pick, since they then have a reason to share an email. Ask first only when you need to follow up with everyone who starts, including those who quit.

faq_plan.q: Can visitors go back and change an answer on a conversational landing page?
faq_plan.a: They can if you build a back button, and you should. A visitor who mistaps company size could otherwise end up on the wrong path. Keep earlier answers filled in when they step back, and work out the path again from the changed answer onward.
